units.title: Can AI Become Human-Compatible?
units.golden:
The challenge is not building smarter AI.
The challenge is building wiser AI.
units.article:
Artificial intelligence is becoming more powerful every year.

AI can help doctors detect diseases, assist teachers in creating personalized lessons, and help scientists analyze large amounts of data.

Because of these benefits, many people believe AI will improve our lives.

However, there is also a concern. What happens if AI pursues goals that do not match human values?

A highly capable AI system might make decisions that are efficient but harmful to people.

The goal is not simply to build smarter AI. The goal is to build AI that works well with humanity.
units.arrow:
Benefits of AI
⇔
Risks of AI
↓
Human-Compatible AI
choices: AI is becoming powerful, so humans should stop using it.
AI can bring benefits, but it must be designed to work well with human values.
AI is useful only for doctors and scientists.
AI will automatically become ethical as it becomes smarter.
units.reflection: If AI became your teacher, doctor, or boss, what rule should it always follow?

units.title: Why Do Humans Procrastinate?
units.golden:
Procrastination is not a time problem.
It is a design problem.
units.article:
Almost everyone procrastinates sometimes.

Students delay homework. Workers postpone important tasks. Even experienced professionals often avoid difficult work.

Many people believe procrastination happens because they are lazy. However, psychologists suggest a different explanation.

The human brain naturally prefers immediate rewards over future rewards.

Checking a message or watching a short video provides instant satisfaction. In contrast, studying for an exam may provide benefits only in the future.

Research shows that changing the environment can be more effective than relying on willpower alone.

The challenge is not becoming a different person. The challenge is designing a better system for yourself.
units.arrow:
Procrastination
↓
Immediate rewards
↓
Environment design
↓
Better action
units.q: Which conclusion best matches the article?
choices: People procrastinate because they are always lazy.
The best way to stop procrastinating is to wait for motivation.
Changing your environment can help you act better.
Future rewards are always stronger than immediate rewards.
units.reflection: What is one distraction you could remove from your study environment today?

units.title: Why Sleep Matters
units.golden:
Sleep is not rest.
Sleep is learning.
units.article:
Many people see sleep as passive time.

When we sleep, we appear to be doing nothing. However, the brain is surprisingly active during sleep.

Researchers have discovered that sleep plays an important role in memory, learning, emotional regulation, and physical recovery.

In one experiment, participants learned a new skill and then slept. Another group learned the same skill but stayed awake.

The group that slept performed significantly better the next day.

During sleep, the brain reorganizes information and strengthens important neural connections.

Sleep is not time lost. Sleep is an investment in tomorrow's performance.
units.q: Which title best matches the article?
choices: How Sleep Supports Learning and Performance
Why Students Should Study All Night
units.reflection: What will you do tonight because of this article?
